topic: Stress Tools 5: One small thing that matters (values)
caption:
It's Thursday night, and the call you meant to make to a friend has slipped again.

When stress crowds the week, try one small thing that matters. Psychologists call this values clarification: naming what matters to you, and why. A recent systematic review of trials found it was often linked with better mood and a stronger sense of meaning. The benefits were more consistent when people acted on their values, not just thought about them. On its own, it didn't ease anxiety or low mood. Its effect on stress itself was mixed.

How to try it today:
1. Pick one value that matters to you. Connection, health, learning, or kindness.
2. Say in one sentence why it matters.
3. Choose one small action today that fits it. A text to a friend, or a ten-minute walk.

Many of the studies were low quality. If stress is wearing you down, you could talk it through with a psychologist.

Save this for a crowded week.

Research:
Napier, A. D., & Mangat, A. (2026). The well-being and ill-being impacts of values clarification: A systematic review of randomised controlled trials. The Journal of Positive Psychology. Advance online publication. https://doi.org/10.1080/17439760.2026.2714053

This content is for general informational purposes and does not constitute psychological advice. If you are experiencing significant distress, please speak with a registered health professional.
